!49 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// Look at the block reached only by the true arm of the branch that tests\0A// `all(uv < 0.5))` (source line 8). The source computes the level-of-detail value\0A// unconditionally, before that branch. In both DXC panes below, the compiled IR places the LOD\0A// calculation itself inside that conditionally-reached block instead -- after the branch, not\0A// before it -- even though nothing about its inputs depends on the branch condition. That is the\0A// illegal code motion the issue reports: the LOD calculation has been sunk into non-uniform\0A// control flow.
